papers.title: Is Low Male Fertility Adaptive? Implications for Male Infertility Research.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Fertile human males produce significantly fewer sperm per gram of testes than most other animals, including primates. Human's low sperm output is associated with a lower pregnancy rate per episode of intercourse and a longer time to pregnancy than in most other species. This, coupled with the concealed nature of ovulation in women, means that human couples frequently require numerous acts of intercourse to achieve a pregnancy. The reason for the low fecundability of humans is unknown. METHODS: I performed a literature review examining the efficiency of spermatogenesis and time to pregnancy in humans to estimate the period of time and average number of episodes of sexual intercourse required for pregnancy. These estimates were corroborated with mathematical models. Hypotheses are suggested to explain the low fecundity of humans. RESULTS: The average, fertile human couple has sexual intercourse 17-35 times over 2-6 months to conceive, with some fertile couples requiring longer periods of time. These numbers and time period are greater than for most other species. Among the theories that could be advanced to explain the relatively low fecundability of humans compared with other species, two will be explored here: (i) a reduction in the risk of pre-eclampsia with repeated sexual intercourse with a single partner over several months and/or (ii) improved pair-bonding from repeated intercourse over time leading to improved outcomes for children. CONCLUSIONS: Reduced sperm production in men may be evolutionarily adaptive. Lower fertility and longer time to conception is associated with a reduced risk of pre-eclampsia and improved outcomes for offspring. Greater understanding of the mechanism(s) involved in the relatively low sperm output in men might provide clues to explain some types of male infertility. Additional research into the reduced efficiency of sperm output in men is warranted.

papers.title: Engagement and outcomes of veterans endorsing suicidal ideation in a couple-based treatment for posttraumatic stress disorder.
papers.abstract: Approximately half of veterans with posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) experience suicidal ideation (SI), and many report intimate relationship problems. Historically, there has been hesitation to engage veterans with SI in PTSD treatment for fear that trauma-focused interventions could potentially exacerbate SI. Additional concerns include that veterans with SI would not be fully psychologically present, engaged in, and benefiting from treatment. This secondary analysis of data from a clinical trial of brief cognitive-behavioral conjoint therapy for PTSD (bCBCT) examines engagement, retention, and PTSD and relationship satisfaction outcomes for 92 veterans and their intimate partners. Veterans were grouped by baseline report of SI in the past year (n = 35) versus no SI (n = 57). Treatment dropout did not significantly differ between veterans who reported SI and those who did not, χ2(1, N = 92) = 0.50, p = .479. Significant reductions in PTSD during treatment were observed for both veterans with, d = -1.34) and without SI, d = -0.87. Partners also reported reductions in veterans' PTSD symptoms for veterans with SI, d = -0.46, and without SI, d = -0.82. PTSD symptom reduction did not differ significantly by SI status according to veteran or partner report. In contrast, we found no evidence of systematic change in relationship satisfaction for veterans or partners regardless of baseline SI status. There were no suicide-related adverse events. The findings suggest that couples in which the veteran endorses SI can engage in and benefit from couple-based PTSD treatment.

papers.title: Unraveling the Ultrafast Photodynamics of Molecular Photoswitches in β-Adrenergic Receptors by First-Principles Nonadiabatic Dynamics Simulations.
papers.journal: Journal of chemical theory and computation
papers.abstract: Understanding how protein environments regulate the photodynamics of chromophores is a central task in quantum biology and remains a major challenge. This challenge is particularly significant for G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs), which are natively nonphotochromic but can be optically controlled via synthetic photoswitchable ligands. Such artificial photoreceptors are new and important because they not only enable the photocontrol of signaling processes beyond those regulated by rhodopsins but also deepen our fundamental understanding of quantum effects in light-protein interactions. However, the ultrafast nonadiabatic dynamics of these ligands in GPCRs remain difficult to resolve experimentally, while traditional computational approaches fail to describe these processes accurately and efficiently. Here, we employed a multiscale framework to comprehensively characterize how receptor binding, mutations, receptor subtype, chemical substitution, and binding pocket electrostatics regulate the photodynamics of photoswitchable antagonists (OPs) of β-adrenergic receptors (β-ARs). This framework integrates extensive first-principles ground-state conformational sampling, absorption-spectra calculations, and nonadiabatic dynamics simulations. Chemical substitutions influence how excitation energy, excited-state lifetimes, and quantum yields (QY) respond to receptor binding, subtype changes, and binding-pocket mutations. The F289A and Y199A mutants generally accelerate excited-state dynamics by reducing local contacts, whereas the D113E mutation slows the dynamics of OP2 in β2-ΑR by reducing the excited-state driving force. Neutralizing the charge of the counterion D113 residue via protonation increases the QY of OP2 in β2-ΑR by altering the local electrostatic and hydrogen-bonding environment. papers.title: How Can I Trust You Again? Repair Behaviours and Trust Recovery After Romantic Betrayal.
papers.journal: Journal of marital and family therapy
papers.abstract: Trust recovery after romantic betrayal is a central concern in couple therapy, yet little is known about which behaviours are most strongly associated with partners' perceived trust repair. We present the results of an online survey of betrayed partners who had attempted reconciliation after romantic infidelity (N = 263). Using hierarchical regressions, we tested for the effect of dispositional predictors (attachment anxiety, attachment avoidance, propensity to trust) and betrayed partners' perceptions of five post-betrayal repair behaviours (transparency, monitoring, remorse, explanation, reconnection) on trust recovery (i.e., differential of trust in the betraying partner now compared to after having discovered the infidelity). Repair behaviours explained substantially more variance in trust recovery than dispositions, which had, at best, rather indirect effects. More specifically, perceived remorse, reconnection, and explanation uniquely predicted trust recovery, whereas transparency and monitoring did not account for additional unique variance once other behaviours were included. These findings suggest trust repair is chiefly associated with what partners do, more than with stable predispositions.

papers.title: Scaling up the 'Art at the Start' parent-infant art therapy intervention: feasibility, acceptability and efficacy.
papers.abstract: AIMS: To evaluate the generalisability of our 'Art at the Start' Parent-Infant Art Therapy intervention by addressing feasibility, acceptability and efficacy across new gallery sites in Scotland. METHODS: We used a participatory action research model with art therapists embedded in galleries, and mixed methods of collecting data, including standardised self-report measures, observation and qualitative feedback. RESULTS/FINDINGS: The Parent-Infant Art Therapy model proved feasible to embed in all sites, with good adherence to the model as well as potential for local adaptation. Families responded well with positive feedback and high rates of uptake, retention and completion of measures. Outcomes showed significant improvement across caregiver wellbeing, perceptions of their relationship to the infant, and observable infant experiences. CONCLUSIONS: Our co-developed creative intervention model generalises beyond the local team, offering a successful approach to supporting public mental health by improving early relationships. Scaling up Art at the Start: a creative group to support infants’ relationshipsArt at the Start developed a model of Parent-Infant Art Therapy groups for infants and their caregivers, using the art process to support their relationship. The model was designed together with families and local partners. We have tested this approach in our local area but wanted to ensure that it worked elsewhere. To do this, we set up new services, with art therapists based in galleries across Scotland working with 0–3s and their caregivers. We look at how these services were set up and whether art therapists were able to follow the model. We look at whether families were happy to be part of the service, their experiences in the groups and whether they were happy to complete the evaluation measures. We also looked at the outcomes of the groups and whether they improved mental health for caregivers and infants.

papers.title: Double halogenation controls the conformation of benzyl alcohol: does DFT fail to predict it even qualitatively?
papers.abstract: Benzyl alcohol and its derivatives can occur in chiral and in more elusive mirror-symmetric structures. ortho-Halogenation (X) couples this structural duality with distorted OH⋯X vs. very weak CH⋯O/CH⋯X hydrogen bonding. We show by a combination of infrared and rotational spectroscopy in supersonic jets that additional para-halogenation introduces a particularly interesting halogen-sensitive conformational preference. While ortho-para-difluorobenzyl alcohol prefers the chiral OH⋯X arrangement, ortho-para-dichlorobenzyl alcohol favors the achiral structure with CH⋯O/CH⋯X contacts. Density functional (exemplified by dispersion corrected B3LYP) calculations fully support the infrared and rotational spectra of the competing conformations, but fail in predicting the energetic switch from F to Cl substitution, even when harmonic zero point energy is added or the electronic energy is replaced by its DLPNO-CCSD(T) counterpart. Only the combined effect of vibrational zero point energy and correlated wavefunction energetics is able to correctly predict the switch to mirror symmetry for Cl. Is there a density functional approach out there that predicts the correct structural switch on its own?

papers.title: Solute-Induced Modulation of Hydrogen Bonding, Ion Hydration, and Protonation in Hydrogels for Enhanced Microwave Absorption.
papers.abstract: Hydrogels have emerged as promising candidates for microwave absorption in next-generation flexible electronics and soft robotics, whose rapid development demands increasingly sophisticated and tunable dielectric properties from microwave-absorbing materials. However, the coupling of hydrogen bonding, ionic coordination, and protonation involving water creates a complex noncovalent interaction network, making it difficult to explore the main contribution of each interaction to the dielectric response, which hinders modulation of dielectric performance. Here, we propose a solute-mediated regulation strategy based on acrylic acid (AA) and acrylamide (AM) backbones by introducing polar groups, metal salts (M+), and acidic solutions (H+) to systematically investigate hydrogen bonding, metal-ion hydration, and protonation in regulating dielectric properties. The results reveal that hydrogen bonding and ionic coordination suppress proton hopping while generating new dipolar polarization units, thereby reducing reflection and shifting the dielectric response from conduction-dominated to polarization-dominated, whereas protonation balances conduction and polarization by regulating water conduction and suppressing hydrogen-bond-induced orientational polarization. Notably, hydrogen bonding coupled with Co(NO3)2-induced hydrated ions and tartaric acid-induced protonation both enabled a broad effective absorption bandwidth (EAB) of 7.1 GHz at thicknesses of 1.88 and 1.85 mm, respectively.

papers.title: Fe/Ni-MIL-101 derived magnetic porous bimetallic-carbon for clean-up and detection of triazole fungicides in fruits and vegetables.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Triazole fungicides are a group of wide-spectrum antifungal pesticides and widely employed in agriculture to combat various fungal diseases. However, their analysis in food remains challenging due to the large amounts of co-extracted interfering species that often compromise analytical accuracy. QuEChERS, which integrates an aqueous-organic partitioning step with a dispersive solid-phase extraction has emerged as a popular sample pretreatment technique for effective interference removal. Accordingly, exploring novel QuEChERS sorbents with simple preparation, adequate clean-up ability, and great feasibility is of crucial significance and great interest. RESULTS: A novel bimetallic magnetic nanoporous carbon (Fe/Ni@MDC) was prepared from Fe/Ni-MIL-101 and applied as a sorbent for QuEChERS of triazole fungicides. Fe/Ni-MIL-101 was first fabricated and then thermally treated under an argon atmosphere to obtain Fe/Ni@MDC. The obtained Fe/Ni@MDC maintained the octahedral structure of MIL-101, a high graphitization degree, nanopores, and superparamagnetism. These properties endowed Fe/Ni@MDC with high adsorption capacities of 501.6 mg/g (chlorophyll), 448.7 mg/g (lutein), and 456.9 mg/g (β-carotene), which are typical interfering pigments in fruits and vegetables; the adsorption capacities were 29.7-48.8-fold higher than those of commercial sorbent GCB. In combination with the superparamagnetism, Fe/Ni@MDC enabled a superfast clean-up of pigment-interfering matrix by magnetic separation within 18 s. Adsorption results and XPS analysis revealed that the mechanism underlying the exceptional QuEChERS performance of Fe/Ni@MDC involved multiple interactions with the target pigments, including π-π stacking, hydrophobic, coordination, and hydrogen bonding interactions. papers.title: Social monitoring predicts future rank and mating success in male macaques.
papers.abstract: In primate societies, much of what matters is revealed by watching others. By attending to the social interactions of group members, individuals may acquire detailed knowledge about prosocial tendencies, alliance networks, and dominance structure,1,2,3 which can inform strategic decisions such as bond and coalition partner choice.4,5 Although allocation of visual attention is a fundamental cognitive process,6,7 its immediate and long-term behavioral consequences remain unclear, leaving ethological and neuroscientific research on social attention5,8,9 largely disconnected from work linking sociality to fitness.10,11 Bridging these research areas has been challenging in part due to the difficulty of quantifying social attention under natural conditions.9,12,13,14 Using a novel social scene protocol for recording visual attention to spontaneously unfolding interactions of nearby group members in the wild,15 we show across 46 adult male macaques that individual differences in visual attention to others' affiliative interactions was associated with male social bond strength later that year. Increased social bond strength, in turn, predicted a male's dominance success in the following year, and ultimately, enhanced male mating success. Post hoc analyses point to interventions in friendly behavior as a plausible behavioral mechanism connecting individual differences in attention with social bonding. In sum, our findings connect two largely siloed bodies of work by providing a chain of evidence linking individual variation in social monitoring to both its effects on the affiliation network and long-term consequences for key correlates of direct fitness.

papers.title: Functional β-cyclodextrin-based adsorbents for the extraction of antibiotic, pesticide, and mycotoxins from food: Preparation, mechanism and applications.
papers.abstract: Food is a fundamental necessity for human growth and survival, while the presence of contaminants such as antibiotic residues, pesticide residues and mycotoxins can affect food quality as well as human health. β-Cyclodextrin (β-CD) is an oligosaccharide containing seven d-glucose units, with a hydrophobic inner cavity and a hydrophilic outer layer. This review provides a critical overview of the development of β-CD-based adsorbents for extracting contaminants from food. Various types of β-CD adsorbents, including crosslinked β-CD polymer, magnetic β-CD adsorbent, β-CD-coupled molecularly imprinted polymer (MIP), β-CD-coupled metal-organic framework (MOF), and β-CD-coupled covalent organic framework (COF), are critically discussed with emphasis on the preparation, characterization, adsorption mechanism and advantages. The major interactions in contaminant extraction include host-guest inclusion, hydrophobic interactions, hydrogen bonding, van der Waals interactions, and electrostatic interactions. The effect of material modification on adsorption behaviour in terms of selectivity, adsorption capacity and efficiency are critically discussed. Finally, challenges related to matrix effects, toxicity, environmental effects, and scale-up issues are highlighted and future prospects for the development of sustainable β-cyclodextrin adsorbents for food contaminant extraction are proposed.

papers.title: Self-transformation and sexual risk-taking: A qualitative study of Iranian women's experiences.
papers.abstract: Within cultural and social structures characterized by gender inequality, women are increasingly exposed to the physical, psychological, and socio-cultural consequences of sexual risk-taking (SRT). In Iran, many women experience their first sexual encounters in a context of normative and institutional constraints and limited power to negotiate their sexual rights and desires, before acquiring the competencies needed to manage sexual risks and prevent their adverse consequences. Drawing on women's lived experiences, this qualitative study explores perceptions of sexual risks and explains the processes of SRT using the 'context-process-outcome' framework. This study focuses on women who had experienced SRT in relationships with their sexual partners. Using constructivist grounded theory, we analyzed interviews with 22 participants aged 22-38 years. The findings reveal a contextual, dynamic, and recursive process of women's SRT that begins with discovering the sexual self and leads to transformation of the overall self. Within this trajectory, SRT functions as a means of attaining agency and fostering intimate and mutually responsible relationships through the integration of sex and attachment and of the sexual self into the overall self. Participants described how gender norms, socio-cultural position, and unbalanced power relations constrained their autonomy during early sexual encounters and undermined their ability to negotiate safer sexual practices. By moving beyond individualistic approaches to sexual health, this study identifies new processes of women's SRT in contemporary Iranian society that may inform context-sensitive sexual health policies and interventions. These insights may also assist counselors and sexual health professionals in providing support that is responsive to women's needs as they navigate this complex journey.

papers.title: Advancing an Integrated Pathway to Child and Youth Mental Health and Substance Use Health Care: A Case Study.
papers.abstract: There is a strong, complex relationship between Mental Health and Substance Use Health (MHSUH). While integrated care is widely recognized as an effective approach to addressing young people's MHSUH needs, there is limited applied evidence on how community-based agencies can collaboratively design, implement, and sustain these models in practice. We conducted a single case study focused on the partnership between a youth mental health and youth substance use health agency to develop and implement an integrated MHSUH service model. Through document analysis (n = 26), interviews (n = 14), and observation notes (n = 2), we examined the process of creating and implementing the model, and key learnings to inform spread and scale of similar initiatives. Data was analyzed using a reflective thematic approach with critical input from the agency leaders. Results highlight the importance of continuous collaboration, commitment, and championing from leadership, and specific resources needed to move integrated models from plans into action.

papers.title: Violent Reinjury Trajectories Across Injury Mechanisms: A Multicenter Cohort Study.
papers.abstract: STUDY OBJECTIVE: Survivors of violent injury often experience reinjury. We sought to identify demographic and clinical factors associated with violent reinjury across different injury types. METHODS: We conducted an observational cohort study of individuals with violent injury (ie, blunt assaults, stabbings, and firearm injuries) across 2 adult and 2 pediatric Level I trauma centers from 2016 to 2023. Covariates included age, sex, race, hospital type, insurance status, and social vulnerability. Our primary outcome was time to reinjury. We used multivariable Cox proportional hazards models to measure associations between each covariate and time to reinjury across injury types. RESULTS: There were 29,038 individuals with nonfatal violent injuries. Male sex (n=19,273; 66.4%), Black and other race (n=21,403; 73.7%), presentation to adult hospitals (n=24,200; 83.3%), public insurance (n=13,879; 47.8%), and living in an area with high social vulnerability (n=21,044; 72.5%) were associated with a greater risk of any violent reinjury, adjusting for covariates. For index firearm injuries, patients younger than18 years had greater risk of firearm reinjury than patients aged 18 to 26 years (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR]:0.65 [0.47 to 0.91]) and for those older than 26 years (aHR:0.47 [0.34 to 0.66]). Although women with firearm injury had a lower risk of firearm reinjury compared with men (aHR:0.46 [0.36 to 0.58]), they had greater risk of blunt reinjury (aHR:1.77 [1.34 to 1.24]). Patients living in areas with high social vulnerability had a higher risk of escalating reinjury mechanism (eg, blunt to firearm; aHR:1.46 [1.11 to 1.90]) versus patients in areas with low/average social vulnerability. CONCLUSION: This research underscores how sequelae of violent reinjury are shaped by certain demographic and clinical characteristics, highlighting opportunities to strengthen reinjury prevention in key subgroups.

papers.title: Sexual and Intimate Partner Violence: A Latent Class Analysis on Victimization Co-Occurrence and Self-Capacities Outcomes Among Women Seeking Sex Therapy.
papers.abstract: Childhood sexual abuse is a significant public health issue associated with an increased risk of revictimization. Although the scientific literature has identified distinct victimization trajectories among women survivors, little is known about potential classes or profiles within clinical samples, and how these classes may differ in terms of survivors' self-capacities (i.e. affect, identity, and relationship functioning). This study aimed to identify classes of interpersonal victimization based on four indicators (i.e. childhood sexual abuse, adult sexual assault, sexual and physical intimate partner violence) among adult women consulting in sex therapy (n = 628). Results of latent class analyses identified three classes: Intimate Partner Victimization (10.7%), Adult Sexual Victimization (38.7%), and Few Victimization Experiences (50.6%). Women in the first class all reported physical intimate partner violence, women in the second class all reported adult sexual assault, and women in the third class reported the lowest numbers of victimization experiences compared to the other two classes. Results showed differences between the classes on altered self-capacities as outcomes. More precisely, women in the Intimate Partner Revictimization class reported significantly higher affect dysregulation and interpersonal conflicts than participants in the other two classes. Findings suggest that altered self-capacities may represent vulnerability factors contributing to the perpetuation of the cycle of revictimization among survivors of childhood sexual abuse.

papers.title: Experiences of Primiparous Women Receiving Breastfeeding Counseling During the Early Postpartum Period: A Qualitative Study.
papers.journal: Breastfeeding medicine : the official journal of the Academy of Breastfeeding Medicine
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Breastfeeding counseling provided by health care professionals is essential for initiating and sustaining breastfeeding. Although its effectiveness is well documented, less is known about women's experiences and emotional responses during the counseling process, particularly in Türkiye, where qualitative evidence remains limited. OBJECTIVE: This study was conducted online with first-time mothers living in the Central Anatolia Region of Türkiye who had received routine breastfeeding counseling from midwives and nurses in public hospitals during the early postpartum period (within the first 4 weeks after birth). MATERIALS AND METHODS: A qualitative descriptive study using inductive content analysis was conducted. Thirteen primiparous women in the early postpartum period (within the first 4 weeks after birth) who had received breastfeeding counseling participated in semistructured interviews via WhatsApp video calls. Participants were recruited using purposive sampling. Data were collected between October and December 2025. RESULTS: Four themes emerged: "Preparing for breastfeeding," "Encountering the reality of breastfeeding," "Breastfeeding within a social context," and "Experiencing breastfeeding counseling and gaining confidence." Women entered the postpartum period with positive expectations regarding breastfeeding but frequently underestimated the physical and emotional challenges they would encounter. Breastfeeding difficulties often resulted in pain, anxiety, guilt, and concerns about maternal competence. Partners and family members served as both supportive and pressuring influences throughout the breastfeeding process. Counseling experiences varied according to health care professionals' communication styles. papers.title: Multilevel Factors Associated with Cannabis Use Disorder in an HIV Status-Neutral Cohort of Young Black Sexual and Gender Minority Adults Assigned Male at Birth-The N2P2 Cohort Study.
papers.journal: Journal of racial and ethnic health disparities
papers.abstract: As cannabis use becomes increasingly prevalent and legally accessible in the United States, cannabis use disorder (CUD) remains an important public health concern for Black sexually minoritized men (SMM) and transgender women (TW), who experience elevated cannabis use and intersecting social and structural stressors that may shape cannabis-related harms. Cross-sectional data were collected from October 2022 to May 2024 in the Chicago metropolitan statistical area to examine individual-level (.e.g., relationship status), interpersonal-level (e.g., social support), and community-level (e.g.., neighborhood safety) correlates associated with CUD [measured by the revised Cannabis Use Disorders Identification Test, (CUDIT-R)]. Guided by the Social Ecological Model, bivariate analyses and logistic regression models were used. A total of 538 participants were included in the analyses, with 52.6% (n = 283) indicating a clinically significant risk of CUD. The mean age of the participants was 27.8 years (SD = 3.84) and most self-identified as cisgender men (83.5%). At the individual level, participants at risk for CUD had higher adjusted odds of using blunts as their primary consumption method (OR = 2.16, 95% CI: 1.31, 3.57) and lower adjusted odds of being in a relationship (OR = 0.61, 95% CI: 0.40, 0.93). Regarding interpersonal differences, participants who screened at risk of CUD had higher adjusted odds of reporting intimate partner violence (aOR 1.58, 95% CI: 1.04, 2.39) than those without CUD. Community factors were not significantly associated with CUD. Longitudinal research is needed to clarify how individual, interpersonal, community, and structural factors interact over time to shape CUD risk in legalized cannabis environments.

papers.title: Age- and sex-specific burden of major depressive disorders and attributable risk factors in high-income regions, 1990-2023.
papers.abstract: Despite the substantial burden of major depressive disorder (MDD) in the GBD-defined high-income super-region, analyses remain limited. Therefore, this study assessed the burden and risk factors of MDD in this super-region. This study estimated MDD burden from 1990 to 2023 using the Global Burden of Disease Study (GBD) 2023. MDD was defined according to the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders and corresponding ICD codes. Age-standardized incidence rates (ASIR) and age-standardized disability-adjusted life years (DALY) rates (ASDR) were calculated with 95% uncertainty intervals (UIs). Sex-specific attributable risk factors were assessed, including sexual violence against children and bullying victimization in both sexes and intimate partner violence additionally in females. In 2023, the ASDR of MDD in the high-income super-region was 675.51 (95% UI, 465.94-940.73) per 100,000 population. The burden peaked among adolescents aged 15-19 years and was generally higher in females, who showed 78.3% higher DALY rates than males. ASIR and ASDR markedly increased between 2019 and 2020 (percent change, ASIR, 49.3%; ASDR, 23.5%), after which ASIR showed a declining trend while ASDR remained relatively stable. Regarding risk factors, bullying victimization accounted for the largest attributable ASDR (57.51 [95% UI, 28.46-98.51] per 100,000 population) among males, whereas intimate partner violence was the leading risk factor among females (104.75 [43.33-178.89]). MDD remains a substantial source of health loss in the high-income super-region, with pronounced disparities by age and sex and persistent disability burden after 2020. These findings may inform targeted prevention strategies, with particular attention to adolescent mental health.
